Depends what kind of restaurant.

Chain places (Applebees, Ruby Tuesday, Elias Bros., TGI Friday's, et al.), and all fast food - all mass-produced, pre-fab food from company vendors. If you get caught making something that didn't come from their production line, they'll boot you and sue you.

AYCE chinese buffets, most regular chinese joints, even most mexican places - almost the entire menu comes in bags from Gordon and Sysco. I've never been to a chinese place where their wonton soup wasn't just pre-fab wontons in hot water with chicken base stirred in and some green onion sprinkled on top. There's a mexican place near me that doesn't even make their own refried beans.

Family diners, local greasy spoons (particularly those that are open for breakfast) - anywhere from 50/50 to 75/25, believe it or not, in favor of hand-made food. Those places run on thin profit margins and it just doesn't pay to shell out $13.95 for a 5lb sack of mashed potatoes when you can get a 50lb sack of Russets and pay some kid $7.50 an hour to come in after school and peel them. Especially when you go through 300lbs of potatoes a week.

Anywhere else, where you'd look out of place (or be refused entry) wearing blue jeans - probably 90-100% hand made food. And the stuff they do buy, like breads, desserts, condiments and the like, are typically going to be of a higher quality or better brand than what most people are accustomed to.
